approved_definition_context: Fin J is the finite index0,...,J-1; J-1 inside a real annotation is real subtraction after coercion. Lagrange.basis(univ,t,j) is the real polynomial product over k!=j of C((t_j-t_k)^(-1))*(X-C(t_k)); ell.eval s is real polynomial evaluation. For distinct nodes this is exactly product(s-t_k)/(t_j-t_k).

sSup is the conditionally complete real supremum. Set.image(F,Icc0h) is the range of F on the closed real interval. Interval integrals are Lebesgue integrals with orientation a..b; all displayed intervals here have nonnegative endpoints in order. Real.cos and Real.pi have their usual meanings.

run(g,eta,eps,y,fuel,x) returns none at zero fuel. At positive fuel it evaluates g(x), next=y-eta*g(x), returns some(x,1) if norm(next-x)<=(1-eta)*eps, otherwise recurses at next with one less fuel and adds one to a successful returned count. Each returned count includes the terminal gradient test. Arithmetic is exact real arithmetic.

collectQueries 0 f=some(empty array,0); collectQueries (m+1) f executes f(0), then recursively the tail f(i.succ), and returns some(Fin.cons(first output,tail outputs),first count+tail count). A failed call propagates none.
The input is ((X,P),((zeta0,zeta1),(G0,G1))). Fin m enumerates exactly m actual nodes; arrays are not source-specific quadrature by definition.

stdGaussian is the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability law; Measure.pi is an independent finite array; prod is the independent product; map is measurable pushforward; IsMarkovKernel requires probability kernels. Integrable means Bochner integrability under its displayed measure. gradient is the real inner-product gradient and finrank real dimension.

The phaseQuery symbol in this theorem is precisely the following paired finite-phase definition, with the same helper context above; the link is definitional, not an extra theorem premise:
{E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
{m : ℕ} (g : E → E) (eta eps h : ℝ)
    (t : Fin m → ℝ) (omega : Fin m → Fin m → ℝ)
    (positionWeight momentumWeight : Fin m → ℝ) (fuel : E → ℕ)
    (w : (E × E) × ((E × E) × ((Fin m → E) × (Fin m → E)))) :
    Option ((E × E) × ℕ) := do
  let P0 := Real.exp (-h/2) • w.1.2 + Real.sqrt (1-Real.exp (-h)) • w.2.1.1
  let Y0 := fun i => w.1.1 + t i • P0
  let r0 ← collectQueries m (fun i =>
    (run g eta eps (Y0 i) (fuel (Y0 i)) (Y0 i)).map
      (fun r => (g (r.1+Real.sqrt eta • w.2.2.1 i),r.2+1)))
  let Y1 := fun i => Y0 i - ∑ j, omega i j • r0.1 j
  let r1 ← collectQueries m (fun i =>
    (run g eta eps (Y1 i) (fuel (Y1 i)) (Y1 i)).map
      (fun r => (g (r.1+Real.sqrt eta • w.2.2.2 i),r.2+1)))
  pure ((w.1.1+h • P0-∑ j, positionWeight j • r1.1 j,
    Real.exp (-h/2) • (P0-∑ j, momentumWeight j • r1.1 j) +
      Real.sqrt (1-Real.exp (-h)) • w.2.1.2),r0.2+r1.2)

ApproximateProximalExecution.proximalQuery(g,eta,eps,y,fuel,x) is exactly the recursive run(g,eta,eps,y,fuel,x) defined above; run is a context abbreviation for that very same Lean function, not a distinct interpreter. CountedPhaseProgram.phaseQuery calls that proximalQuery function for both finite arrays.
